svg.title: Giza Planets Simulation
svg.text: Schematic reconstruction. Magnitudes are typical values; for exact positions set date/time/location in Stellarium (stellarium.org).
· Venus, Jupiter, Saturn are always on/near the ecliptic, so they
regularly appear in the same part of the sky.
· Jupiter–Saturn conjunctions recur about every 20 years; Venus
passes both yearly-ish (synodic 584 d). Close 3-planet groupings
occur every few years, not once per 2,373 years.
· Visibility depends on date, elongation and horizon: verify in Stellarium.
